claims.claim_text: The indexed Enis H Pike row is linked at high confidence to the uncommon-name career Army officer documented by a reputable obituary.
claims.evidence_excerpt: retired from the United States Army having served in World War II
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary documents the rare exact full name, compatible age, and Army service in World War II and Korea.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact name, middle initial, Army officer career, and compatible World War II service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary establishes wartime Army identity but does not date OSS entry or identify a civilian pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: Later employment at Texas public safety and Sears is postwar and deliberately excluded.

claims.claim_text: The indexed John A Pillepich row is linked at high confidence to Norwich alumnus and Army officer John Andrew Pillepich.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1940 university masthead supplies the rare full name and class year; a 1946 university record identifies the same alumnus as a first lieutenant.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exceptionally rare exact surname, matching given name and middle initial, full middle name, class year, and independently documented Army officer status.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1940 university source documents prewar student status. The 1946 Army address is identity corroboration only.
claims.match_notes: The 1946 military posting is not classified as a pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: John Andrew Pillepich was a Norwich University student and Guidon assistant editor in November 1940.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Norwich Guidon masthead lists him among assistant editors and identifies the class of 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the rare full name, middle initial, class year, and later institutional Army officer record.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented on 14 November 1940, before the OSS was established; no claim of immediacy is made.
claims.match_notes: Norwich is modeled as a student affiliation, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: A contemporary Texas newspaper documents an Edward F. Pilley as a resident engineer in February 1942; row-level identity remains unresolved.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The road-contract article identifies Edward F. Pilley as resident engineer but does not name an employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable exact-name lead, qualified because the index contains two adjacent identical rows and no row-specific identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar on 19 February 1942; not shown to be immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: No employer is inferred, and the two index rows remain separate in a possible-duplicate group.
